reference_sql:
WITH last_orders AS (  -- one row per customer
  SELECT customer_id, MAX(CAST(order_ts AS DATE)) AS last_day
  FROM orders
  WHERE customer_id IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY customer_id
)
SELECT COUNT(*) AS lapsed_customers
FROM last_orders
WHERE DATE '2026-01-05' - last_day > 180
alternatives:
SELECT COUNT(*) AS lapsed_customers
FROM (  -- one row per lapsed customer
  SELECT customer_id
  FROM orders
  WHERE customer_id IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY customer_id
  HAVING DATE '2026-01-05' - MAX(CAST(order_ts AS DATE)) > 180
) AS t

WITH last_orders AS (  -- one row per customer
  SELECT customer_id, MAX(order_ts) AS last_ts
  FROM orders
  WHERE customer_id IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY customer_id
)
SELECT COUNT(*) AS lapsed_customers
FROM last_orders
WHERE date_diff('day', last_ts, DATE '2026-01-05') > 180

other_way.sql:
SELECT COUNT(*) AS lapsed_customers
FROM (  -- one row per lapsed customer
  SELECT customer_id
  FROM orders
  WHERE customer_id IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY customer_id
  HAVING DATE '2026-01-05' - MAX(CAST(order_ts AS DATE)) > 180
) AS t
other_way.tradeoff: Filtering the groups with HAVING in a derived table needs no named step, but the CTE shows each customer's last day first.
